state.background: Fresh B3c plan reassessment, preserving the previous JEV-approved B3c plan and its request/response as historical. B3c contains two named Browser Mode cases. The CAGR candidate is p45-a-cagr-sheet-02, actual CagrPanel plus actual useCagrState with deterministic chart data, covering P42-046–049: dialog visible initially and after start-year change, calculated result visible, and rendered result matching /^-?\d+\.\d{2}%$/. Actual route/section trigger P42-040/-041 remains E2E. The desktop Escape candidate is p45-b-tooltip-dismiss-578-chromium-escape-dismiss, P42-577 only. Oracle found the prior plan had a blocking gap: it did not require the actual desktop chart tooltip controller and event handlers, allowing direct state/tooltip activation instead of testing desktop hover-to-dismiss. The corrected plan requires actual nominal SpendingBarChart wired to actual useChartTooltipController({ suppressed: false, isTouch: false }) via tooltipProps and the chart event props onPointerDown, onPointerMove, onMouseMove, onPointerLeave, and onMouseLeave. A real Browser Mode pointer hover over a rendered bar must activate the controller and show the tooltip; send a real Escape key with the established userEvent.keyboard("{Escape}") Browser Mode API and assert the tooltip hides. Never set activeChartId, tooltip active state, or tooltip content directly. This case proves component/controller behavior only. Keep P42-575/-576, P42-578–583 (re-hover, mouseleave, heading/bounds, outside-click), P42-603/-604 and remaining route/coordinate assertions in E2E. Candidate test files are tests/browser-mode/CagrPanel.browser.test.tsx and tests/browser-mode/SpendingBarChart-tooltip-dismiss.browser.test.tsx. Keep A=123/E=90/M=1 and no E2E before all ten new named Batch3 Browser Mode cases pass.
acceptanceCriteria: The CagrPanel.browser.test.tsx candidate mounts the actual CagrPanel and actual useCagrState with deterministic data, shows the dialog initially and after a start-year change, calculates, and asserts the visible rendered result matches /^-?\d+\.\d{2}%$/ for P42-046–049; this is not hook-math-only coverage.
The CAGR route/section trigger and production integration assertions P42-040/-041 remain E2E.

The SpendingBarChart-tooltip-dismiss.browser.test.tsx candidate mounts actual nominal SpendingBarChart with actual useChartTooltipController({ suppressed: false, isTouch: false }) and wires tooltipProps plus onPointerDown, onPointerMove, onMouseMove, onPointerLeave, and onMouseLeave through actual chart event props.

A real Browser Mode pointer hover over an actual rendered bar activates the controller and makes the tooltip visible; the test then sends Escape with the established userEvent.keyboard("{Escape}") API and asserts the tooltip becomes hidden.

The candidate never assigns activeChartId, tooltip active state, or tooltip content directly. It is limited to component/controller behavior and does not claim route integration, production coordinate geometry, or full desktop E2E behavior.

P42-577 is the only proposed assertion transfer for the tooltip stable row. P42-575/-576, P42-578–583 including re-hover, mouseleave, heading/bounds and outside-click, P42-603/-604, and remaining route/coordinate assertions remain in Playwright.
The previous Oracle finding is addressed by requiring the actual desktop controller and event handler path; the two candidate tests do not complete either stable row. Preserve A=123, E=90, M=1.
No Playwright/E2E command runs until all ten new Batch3 named Browser Mode cases pass.
verification: Explorer source mapping: src/app/components/SpendingBarChart.tsx accepts tooltipProps and onPointerDown/onPointerMove/onMouseMove/onPointerLeave/onMouseLeave and forwards these props into its chart; src/app/components/charts/useChartTooltipProps.tsx exports useChartTooltipController and its bind result supplies these event handlers and tooltipProps.

Escape source/API evidence: useChartTooltipProps.tsx handles document keydown Escape; tests/browser-mode/ChartInfoButton.browser.test.tsx imports userEvent from vitest/browser and sends Escape with userEvent.keyboard("{Escape}").

CAGR source mapping: shared_plan/42-assertion-callsite-ledger.md maps P42-046–049 to the dialog/result behavior and P42-040/-041 to actual route-trigger/section integration. Current E2E result matcher is /^-?\d+\.\d{2}%$/.

Tooltip source mapping: P42-577 is the desktop Escape dismissal assertion; surrounding P42-575/-576 and P42-578–583 remain the actual hover/visibility/re-hover/mouseleave/heading/bounds/outside-click guarantees. P42-603/-604 and the remaining route/coordinate assertions are retained as well.

Oracle found the prior plan's omission of actual desktop controller/event-handler wiring to be a blocking plan gap and recommended the specific corrected controller-driven pointer-hover then Escape contract. The corrected plan states this behavior and its strict component-only boundary.
knownConstraints: The CAGR component fixture does not prove P42-040/-041 route/section trigger integration or production data wiring.
The tooltip fixture does not prove production route integration, production coordinate geometry, or all pointer/touch/browser-engine conditions; retained Playwright assertions remain necessary.
Browser Mode emits a real DOM/chart path, but the plan must not bypass controller behavior by setting activeChartId or tooltip active/content state.
B3c remains a two-case partial assertion batch and does not change A/E/M. Do not run E2E before the ten-new-case gate.
state.outputRequirement: Select exactly one plan criterion. If not valid_as_defined, provide a case-specific finding, affected Plan45 location or requirement, observed source evidence, and a concrete proposed fix or exact needed evidence. State remaining uncertainty explicitly. Assess only the corrected B3c plan; preserve prior approval as historical and do not treat this request as implementation or test evidence.

plan.instructions: Assess whether the corrected B3c plan closes Oracle's controller-wiring gap, maps the two assertion slices precisely, retains production E2E boundaries, and preserves the ten-case E2E gate. Select exactly one criterion and give a case-specific diagnosis for any non-pass answer.

criteria.valid_as_defined: The corrected staged plan is internally consistent with the source mapping and acceptance boundaries.
criteria.requirements_mismatch: The plan conflicts with an applicable requirement; identify and correct it.
criteria.missing_prerequisites_info: Required source or scope information is missing; identify it exactly.
criteria.incomplete_implementation_info: The supplied plan context is too incomplete to assess; specify what is needed.
criteria.implementation_issue: A concrete implementation issue is established; identify its evidence and correction.
criteria.scope_violation: The proposal exceeds or violates scope; identify the boundary and adjustment.
criteria.other: A material plan concern does not fit the listed categories; give its finding and fix or evidence needed.
criteria.indeterminate: The supplied context cannot support a reliable plan judgment; identify missing context.
